title: Chester Campbell's father, a tuba player in Harlem bands
summary: Campbell describes his father, who played E-flat tuba, came to New York in 1926, and gigged with Harlem bandleaders.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: My dad, Chester Campbell, Sr., was born in Cumberland, Maryland. He was an orphan and the man that raised him taught him to play the E-flat tuba.

He went on the road with a show called, In Old Kentucky when he was a youngster and in 1926 he brought his bride, Eleanor Campbell and his four youngsters to New York. He played with Cliff Jackson, he played a stint with Earl Hines, he played a stint with Cab Calloway. He switched to the string bass around the early 30s and he took lessons from a German fella for $2.00 a lesson in the front room of our home.
Where was your home at that time?
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

My home was on 148th Street and (inaudible) Avenue. My dad gigged with John C. Smith, Ed Bonelli (phonetically), he made a living, he was a great father to me and he taught me the string bass. He passed on to Glory in 1965 and he left me a legacy.
